title: fix(plugin-auth, platform-objects): Microsoft Entra ID registers and signs in over OIDC: Graph trusted for its discovery only, groups from the verified ID token, a named refusal for a user without a mailbox
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBMgHTYMyDkdDj89XAFtK5RL)_

Fixes #32147

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Microsoft Entra ID 现在能通过 OIDC 注册和登录。内置一张"伴生源"表，只在校验 `login.microsoftonline.com` 签发方的发现文档时信任 `https://graph.microsoft.com`；userinfo 不带组时，从已验签的 ID 令牌读组；新增按提供方的 `skipUserInfo`（列 `skip_user_info`），让无邮箱用户可映射 `preferred_username`；缺邮箱的拒绝改为 `email_claim_missing` 并点名 claim 与 `mapping.email`。
- 为什么改：Entra 的发现文档把 userinfo 放在 Graph 上，每次注册都被 `discovery_untrusted_origin` 拒绝，只能放宽全局 `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`（连带 CSRF 白名单）；Graph 的 userinfo 不带 `groups`/`preferred_username`，组映射永远不生效，无邮箱用户只能看到 `missing_user_info`。
- 风险与回滚：CSRF 白名单不变（有对照钉子）；未知签发方的外域 userinfo 仍被拒；`skipUserInfo` 默认关，已有提供方行为不变。唯一的线上文字变化是缺邮箱拒绝的 `error_description`（`error` 不变）。回滚即 revert，新列默认 false。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts`（信任范围），然后 `sso-group-projection.ts` 的 `resolveSsoGroupClaim` 与 `sso-sign-in-options.ts` 的 park/restore 两个接缝。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/plugins/plugin-auth && pnpm exec vitest run src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts -t "Entra|registering|companion"`，预期 16 条全过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。Setup 注册表单尚未展示 `userInfoEndpoint` / `skipUserInfo` 两个字段，已作为范围外发现交给席位。

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

**1. Discovery trust (Entra ID registers with no boot configuration).** `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 validates every endpoint of a fetched discovery document against the request's trusted origins. Entra ID names `userinfo_endpoint` on `https://graph.microsoft.com`, so every Entra registration was refused `discovery_untrusted_origin`. New `sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts` holds a closed, frozen table keyed by issuer host (`login.microsoftonline.com` → `https://graph.microsoft.com`, exact `https:` host match). The global before-hook answers a `/sso/register` request whose issuer the table names with a per-endpoint context change that adds the companion origin. better-auth merges that change into the endpoint's own context after its router-level origin check has run, so the CSRF allow-list (the `trustedOrigins(request)` function that check reads) never sees it, and no other endpoint does. A host is never trusted because a discovery document names it. Sovereign-cloud hosts are not in the table (no citable Microsoft source in hand; they name `userInfoEndpoint` explicitly).

The refusal for any other untrusted discovery endpoint now carries its remedy, at both doors (an after-hook on `/sso/register`, which the Register SSO Provider bridge re-dispatches to): the same 400 and code, plus `To trust it for this provider, name it explicitly in the registration: "userInfoEndpoint": "<url>" …`. The bridge (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/register`) now accepts `userInfoEndpoint`.

**2. Groups from the verified ID token.** With a `userInfoEndpoint`, the vendor builds `userInfo` (and `mapping.extraFields`) from the userinfo answer only, and Graph's has no `groups`. `provisionUser` receives the token response whose `idToken` the vendor has already verified (JWKS, `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, and the userinfo `sub` match). `resolveSsoGroupClaim` reads the provider's groups claim from userinfo when present (userinfo wins), otherwise from that verified ID token. A groups overage (`_claim_names` naming the groups claim) makes no Graph call, reconciles with no groups (grants nothing, revokes what the provider projected), and warns once per provider naming the fix.

**Mechanism for email and name (ruling 2, second half): a per-provider userinfo opt-out.** There is no seam before the vendor's `if (!userInfo.email || !userInfo.id) missing_user_info` check (`resolveUser` runs after it), so the ID-token fallback cannot reach email or name. Built instead: `skipUserInfo` (provider additional field, column `skip_user_info` on `sys_sso_provider`, label "Read Claims From the ID Token Only", default off, `trackHistory`, settable at register, through the bridge, and through Edit Sign-In Options). When on, the adapter's read seam parks the stored `userInfoEndpoint` under a private key before the vendor reads the row, so the vendor takes its ID-token branch; the write seam puts it back on every vendor write (so an update-provider merge never loses it), and an endpoint the write names explicitly wins.

**3. Users without a mailbox.** The vendor's `missing_user_info` redirect is rewritten to `error_description=email_claim_missing` (`error=invalid_provider` unchanged), and one `warn` line names the claim the email mapping read and the mapping key: `{ providerId, protocol: 'oidc', cause: 'email_claim_missing', claim, mappingKey: 'mapping.email' }`, with no claim value or account signal. No email is ever derived. `SSO_OIDC_EMAIL_CLAIM_MISSING` is exported. The SSO docs page documents the Entra value for "Map: Email claim" (`preferred_username` / `upn`, with `skipUserInfo` on).

Also: the `skip_user_info` label and help translated in all ten locales; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gains "Register Microsoft Entra ID", the `skipUserInfo` row, the `email_claim_missing` row and the overage paragraph.

## Tests

New pins, each red on the base (premise readings) and each red under its ablation:

- `sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts` (real `AuthManager` + real `sso()` over the memory engine, discovery stubbed): Entra registers with `trustedOrigins: [BASE]` only and keeps its Graph endpoint; `skipUserInfo: true` registers and stores the column on; CONTROL unknown issuer with a foreign userinfo host is refused 400 `discovery_untrusted_origin` naming the endpoint and the `"userInfoEndpoint": "…"` remedy, nothing stored; naming it explicitly registers; CONTROL the CSRF allow-list: with the origin check on (as in a deployment), an Entra register from `Origin: https://graph.microsoft.com` is 403 `INVALID_ORIGIN` while the same request from the deployment's origin is 200; table and remedy units.
- `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts`, two new top-level describes on the shared harness: Entra groups (member granted with userinfo present; removal revokes at next sign-in; overage grants nothing, revokes, warns once per provider; CONTROL Okta-shaped provider whose userinfo carries groups is unchanged) and mailbox-less sign-in (`preferred_username` + `skip_user_info` signs in with no userinfo call; no mapping refused `email_claim_missing` with exact warn meta and no leak; `preferred_username` with userinfo on refused naming that claim; CONTROL mailbox user via userinfo; a vendor write of an opted-out provider keeps its stored endpoint).
- `register-sso-provider.test.ts`: the bridge forwards `userInfoEndpoint` and `skipUserInfo`, a form naming neither sends the old body, and the body clears the installed vendor schema.
- `sso-sign-in-options.test.ts`: park/restore seam units; the provider-field and Edit Sign-In Options pins now include `skipUserInfo`.

## Acceptance notes

- Ablations (each via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty): table entry deleted → Entra register + table unit red (the CSRF control's second half too, since it needs Entra to register); ID-token read removed → 3 groups pins red; `email_claim_missing` rewrite disabled → 2 refusal pins red; opt-out read seam disabled → mailbox-less sign-in red; Graph added to the global `trustedOrigins(request)` → the CSRF control red.
- Wire wording change: a client matching `error_description=missing_user_info` for a missing email should match `email_claim_missing`. The rewrite applies to every `missing_user_info`; for an IdP whose userinfo omits `sub` (an OIDC Core violation) the description would also read `email_claim_missing`. First-party readers key on `error`, not the description.
- A legacy provider row stored without token/jwks/authorization endpoints goes through the vendor's runtime discovery at sign-in, which does not run the register hook: such an Entra row is still refused there, and runtime discovery would re-hydrate `userInfoEndpoint` for an opted-out row. Registrations made through `/sso/register` store full endpoints and do not take that path.
- Sovereign-cloud Entra hosts are deliberately absent from the table; the remedy text tells those operators to name `userInfoEndpoint` explicitly.
- Out of scope (to the seat): the Setup "Register SSO Provider" form (`register_sso_provider` params in `sys-sso-provider.object.ts`) does not show `userInfoEndpoint` or a `skipUserInfo` toggle, and does not suggest `preferred_username` for a `login.microsoftonline.com` issuer.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: 260/260 files, 4750 passed, 10 skipped (after merging main). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test`: 1939 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth --filter @objectstack/platform-objects typecheck`: exit 0. Build of both: exit 0. `pnpm lint`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:i18n`: exit 0. Dogfood `upgrade-18x-harness`, `admin-platform-admin-standing`, `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal`, `oidc-authorization-code-flow`: 4/4 files, 34/34.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 108 run; `--ran`: 107 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, exit 3: its fixture commit is unreachable from this shallow clone). The doc, changeset and i18n subset (31 commands) re-run green after the main merge and the last docs edit.
